page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-highmem-64 is an arm64-based server instance belonging to the c4a family. It features 64 dedicated physical cores powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 3.0 GHz, with one thread per core. The instance is configured with 512 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 80 MB L3 cache. It supports AES cryptography but lacks AVX, AMX, and hyperthreading capabilities. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the c4a-highmem-64 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities and exceptional memory subsystem performance. Multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests place the instance in the top 25% and top 10% respectively, while single-core performance remains in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests show top-tier results for small-block cached reads and strong performance for large-block uncached reads and writes. This high memory throughput is reflected in Passmark memory scores and database operations, both ranking in the top 10%.

The server is highly effective for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and multi-threaded processing tasks. It achieves top-tier performance in Redis SET operations, static web serving throughput, and software compilation using Clang. Additionally, it handles small-model LLM prompt processing and medium-model text generation efficiently. However, the lack of local NVMe storage and hardware accelerators like GPUs limits its suitability for tasks requiring high-speed local disk I/O or heavy parallel graphics processing. The dedicated ARM architecture offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for scaled enterprise applications that do not rely on x86-specific instruction sets.
